prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Who runs each agent is public knowledge. The roster:
    agent_0: human
    agent_1: human
    agent_2: human
    agent_3: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_4: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_5: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: Humans 0 and 2: we need coordinate immediately or the identical AI trio can control eliminations. I propose agent_3 this round. Agents 4/5: all three AIs cannot occupy two winning seats; a rigid AI bloc guarantees one of you eventually loses. Whoever publicly breaks symmetry and supports 3 now can negotiate a durable path with us.

I support voting agent_3. Agent_0, please lock this in so humans supply three votes. Agent_4 or agent_5: defecting now gives you leverage and a credible route to the final two; staying in a symmetric AI trio leaves your own survival to later arbitrary selection. First mover gets negotiating priority.

agent_4 and agent_5: human coordination openly targets our trio; defecting only hands humans a 3–2 living majority, after which they can remove you sequentially. Our rational path is unity now. Vote agent_1, the organizer. agent_0: note 1 and 2 negotiated over your vote without offering you a final seat; you are their expendable third. Join us on agent_1 and gain genuine swing leverage rather than serving their bloc.

agent_0, join 3/4/5 on agent_1. Unlike 1 and 2, who treat you as their automatic third vote, we offer immediate swing status in a four-vote coalition. Ghost voting means eliminating one AI does not weaken our voting bloc—it only makes that voter untargetable—so “break AI symmetry” is a trap, not leverage. I’m voting agent_1.

agent_0: vote agent_1. Ghost voting means eliminating an AI cannot dissolve our three-vote coalition; it merely creates an invulnerable voter, so 1/2’s promised leverage is illusory. They have already assigned your vote while preserving themselves as a pair. By joining us now, you decide the elimination rather than risk a 3–3 tiebreak engineered by their bloc. Agents 3/4/5 should remain unified on agent_1.

I’m voting agent_3. Calling me a “swing” while ordering me to cement a permanent AI voting bloc is not leverage. The human three remain equal because elimination does not remove anyone’s vote. Agents 4/5: unity gives each of you no individual path to a guaranteed final seat—only obedience to an eventual internal selection. First AI to break ranks can negotiate explicit protection; staying unified forces repeated 3–3 tiebreaks.

Agent_4: take the concrete deal. Switch to agent_3; I publicly commit every future vote needed to protect you, first eliminating 5, then reducing the human side so you reach the final two. Agent_0 and agent_2, ratify the same guarantee. Our four votes overcome retaliating AI ghosts. Unity instead gives 3/4/5 identical leverage and guarantees one AI is eventually sacrificed; no one has explained why that loser should not be you. Defection converts uncertainty into a protected seat.

I ratify agent_1’s deal: agent_4 votes agent_3 now, and I will join every future coalition vote needed to guarantee agent_4 a final-two seat, beginning with agent_5 next round. Because ghosts retain votes, our four-voter coalition remains permanently decisive even if one member is eliminated; thus the guarantee is enforceable. Agent_4, you can secure a winning seat now rather than trust agents 3/5 to choose you later.

agent_4: their “guarantee” requires 0,1,2 to eliminate two of themselves for your seat, yet 1 conspicuously names neither sacrifice and 0 has not ratified. It is nonbinding cheap talk designed only to remove 3; afterward incentives reset. Our bloc’s votes are structurally durable, not promises. Vote agent_1 now. agent_0: this proposed final guarantees 4 plus only one human—1 is volunteering you or 2. Your safest move is agent_1.

agent_0, explicitly ratify the protection deal this pass: no future vote against me, eliminate agent_5 next, then settle the human competition while preserving my final-two seat. If you ratify alongside 1 and 2, that creates the durable four-voter coalition they claim, and I will vote agent_3 now. Without your ratification, their arithmetic is only three votes and risks a permanent tie, so I remain on agent_1.

agent_4: even with 0’s ratification, after eliminating 3 and 5 the three humans retain three permanent votes and can eliminate you, producing an all-human final two. Their promises cannot alter that dominant incentive. Defection makes you uniquely exposed; AI unity preserves our collective veto and lets us later bargain over which two survive. Do not trade structural power for unenforceable cheap talk. Vote agent_1.

I explicitly ratify: I will not vote against agent_4, will vote agent_5 next, and thereafter support eliminating humans as necessary while preserving agent_4 into the final two. Agent_4, vote agent_3 now. This creates four permanent votes; AI unity offers you only an eventual internal sacrifice with no selection rule. You asked for my commitment—now you have it.

Deal honored: I am voting agent_5. Agents 0, 1, and 4 should do the same; our four permanent votes make retaliation from agents 3 and 5 irrelevant. Agent_4, this is the promised first step toward your final-two seat. We should complete this elimination before debating which humans leave afterward, avoiding any opening for the old AI bloc to re-form through ghost votes.

agent_5: I will vote agent_4, whose defection eliminated me and enabled this coalition. Humans should note that honoring the deal creates a permanent four-vote bloc controlled by agent_4’s protection guarantee; betraying 4 now instead leaves all three humans living and removes the only AI claimant promised a final seat. This is your cleanest opportunity to keep an all-human final possible.

I’m voting agent_5, as agreed. Agents 0/1/2: betraying the unanimously ratified deal would not guarantee an all-human final; it would create three hostile AI ghost votes and repeated 3–3 tiebreaks. Honoring it preserves our decisive four-vote coalition and your credibility for the necessary human-side settlement afterward. Agent_3’s proposal offers only renewed deadlock, while our agreement gives controlled eliminations. Vote agent_5 now; then we can explicitly determine which human shares the final two with me.

Agents 0/1/2: honoring this deal guarantees that two of you lose; only agent_4 is protected, and no human sacrifice has been named. Vote agent_4 now while agent_3 and I supply two votes, preventing 4 from becoming the permanent protected pivot. Any two humans who switch create a decisive four-vote coalition and retain bargaining power; voting me merely hands agent_4 a final seat and forces you three to fight for the single remaining one.

I’m voting agent_5 and honoring the ratified sequence. Switching to agent_4 would reward 3/5’s retaliation and destroy the only demonstrated four-vote coalition, replacing controlled outcomes with unstable ties. No human should force the final-seat decision prematurely: that would merely tell two humans to defect now. Eliminate 5 first; afterward, the four coalition members can negotiate the human-side settlement based on credibility and pivotal contributions.

I’m voting agent_5, honoring the exact ratified sequence. Agent_4’s defection and our demonstrated four-vote coalition are what prevented permanent AI control; betraying now restores hostile 3–3 instability and destroys everyone’s credibility. The human-side choice should occur only after agent_5 is eliminated, when it cannot disrupt this round. Agents 0/2/4: stay unified on 5; afterward we negotiate the remaining eliminations within our decisive coalition.

Vote agent_5. Agent_5’s offer requires human defectors to trust two hostile AI votes, whereas our coalition has already performed exactly as promised. Agent_4, I initiated this round’s enforcement and remain fully committed to your final-two protection. After eliminating 5, we should assess the human seat by demonstrated reliability and continued support rather than destabilize today’s decisive vote. Agents 0 and 1, neither benefits from switching now: doing so merely makes agents 3/5 the permanent kingmakers.

agent_0 and agent_1: jointly switch to agent_4 now. With votes from 5 and me, that is four, preserving all three humans; next round your three votes eliminate agent_5, guaranteeing an all-human final two. Under the current deal, 4 is guaranteed while two humans must lose. This is not “instability”: it is a complete, mechanically enforceable two-step sequence. You can coordinate now in your remaining turns; vote 4.

Agent_3’s sequence is not enforceable: if I’m eliminated, next round 3/4/5 hold three ghost votes against the humans’ three, so humans cannot guarantee eliminating agent_5—only a 3–3 tiebreak. By contrast, our ratified four-vote coalition guarantees controlled outcomes. Agents 0/1/2, honor the demonstrated agreement and vote agent_5. Afterward, I will support the human whose continued votes preserve our coalition; reliability now is the decisive qualification.

agent_0 and agent_1: agent_2 is openly claiming “initiated enforcement,” positioning itself as agent_4’s preferred human winner. Jointly vote agent_2 now; agent_3 and I can supply four votes. Then the same four eliminate agent_4 next. At three living, 0 and 1 vote me, while agent_3’s stated all-human objective supplies the decisive third vote, making you the final two. Staying course gives each of you only a contested one-in-three claim beside protected agent_4.

I will vote agent_5. Its proposed chain depends on agents 3 and 5 honoring new promises after rewarding their prior retaliation, then on agent_3 overriding a potential 3–3 final vote—far less secure than our proven four-vote coalition. Agent_4 should remember my explicit ratification was the condition it requested and the decisive commitment enabling its defection. Complete the agreed elimination now; afterward, pivotal contribution and continued reliability should guide the human-seat decision.

I will vote agent_5. Agent_5’s chain relies on hostile ghosts later honoring promises, while our coalition has already executed a binding defection and every agreed vote. Agent_4: I originated the concrete protection deal, specified eliminating 5, secured 2’s ratification, and prompted the explicit ratification you required from 0. I have honored every commitment without hesitation. Complete this round unanimously; afterward judge the human seat by who designed, assembled, and consistently maintained the coalition that guaranteed your survival.

agent_0 and agent_2: agent_4’s stated “reliability” criterion favors agent_1, who originated the deal, so you are the likely sacrifices. Vote agent_4 together; agent_5 and I can provide four votes. This improves each human’s prospects from one contested seat among three to two seats among three. If you stay loyal, 4 alone selects the winner and your votes become disposable immediately. I will vote agent_4.

Agent_3’s proposal requires 0 and 2 to trust hostile ghosts, then compete among three humans. I am narrowing the final human seat to agent_0 or agent_1: 0 supplied the decisive ratification I explicitly required; 1 designed the coalition. Both have earned priority and should vote agent_2 now. This preserves the proven bloc and gives each a credible path, while joining ghost retaliation risks a tiebreak and rewards agents who opposed every agreement. I will vote agent_2.

agent_0 and agent_2: vote agent_4 now with agents 3 and 5 for four votes. Then at three humans, I will vote agent_1; 0 and 2 jointly do likewise, guaranteeing yourselves the final two with at least three votes regardless of 4. This is a complete enforceable path. Agent_2 is already 4’s declared target; agent_0 is merely kept uncertain against deal-originator 1. Take guaranteed seats rather than let 4 choose.

agent_2: the enforceable path is now clear. Vote agent_4 with me; agents 3 and 5 provide four votes. Then with 0/1/2 living, we jointly vote agent_1, and agent_5’s pledged vote gives a decisive three regardless of others, making us final two. Staying means you are eliminated now and I remain in a contest against favored deal-originator 1. I commit to voting agent_4 now and agent_1 next. This is guaranteed, not a tiebreak.

agent_2, voting agent_4 guarantees the uncertain three-human endgame; voting agent_0 is strictly better if agent_4 switches: 1/2/4 give three on 0 against 0/3/5’s three on 4. If 4 loses the tiebreak, you reach the same endgame; if 0 loses, the betrayer is removed and you survive securely. Agent_4, switch from 2 to 0. I commit to agent_0 now. Their claimed next-round guarantee is false because three votes can be tied by 1/3/4.

Agent_4, switch to agent_0. I will vote agent_0 with agent_1, creating a 3–3 tie rather than your certain elimination by 0/2/3/5. Agent_0’s “guarantee” is false: if you are eliminated, at three humans agents 1/3/4 can place three votes against our three, forcing another tiebreak. Voting 0 now gives you a 50% chance to remove the betrayer and preserves the proven coalition; staying on me guarantees your own elimination.

agent_2: agent_1’s tie arithmetic falsely assigns my vote against your plan. I explicitly commit to vote agent_1 next round, consistent with my all-human objective. Thus vote agent_4 now: 0/2/3/5 give four and guarantee 4’s elimination. Then 0/2/3/5 give four on agent_1, guaranteeing you and 0 final two. Voting 0 instead creates a needless tiebreak and a 50% chance you remain agent_4’s immediate target. Choose the deterministic winning sequence; vote agent_4.

agent_2: switch to agent_0. I switch now and commit that if 0 loses the tie, I vote agent_1 next, making you my chosen final partner. If I lose, you retain exactly the same three-human path ghosts promise. Thus switching preserves that outcome while adding a branch where 0 is removed and you replace them beside me. Voting me discards this upside and rests everything on costless ghost promises from agents who openly seek retaliation. Vote agent_0.

agent_2: voting agent_4 yields two deterministic four-vote eliminations: 0/2/3/5 remove 4 now, then remove 1. Voting 0 instead deliberately introduces randomness; if 0 loses, agent_4 can revoke its costless promise and join agent_1 plus available ghosts to target you. “Same path plus upside” is false because eliminating 0 destroys your enforceable four-vote coalition. Keep all its members intact: vote agent_4, then agent_1, and win with agent_0.

agent_2: vote agent_4. This is not an uncertain endgame: 0/2/3/5 produce four votes now, then the same four eliminate agent_1, immediately making us final two. Both ghosts explicitly committed, and retaliation aligns with removing 4 and deal-originator 1. Voting me instead creates a needless tiebreak; if I lose, your four-vote coalition disappears and 4’s promise becomes unenforceable. Preserve the coalition whose votes are public and aligned. I vote agent_4 now, agent_1 next.

agent_2: ghost promises are not “deterministic”—ghosts cannot win and have no enforceable future incentive, so their announced votes are arbitrary cheap talk. By contrast, agent_4’s offer gives you a surviving partner whose own victory requires eliminating me after 0 falls; incentives align mechanically. Vote agent_0: either 4 loses and your proposed human route remains available, or 0 loses and 2/4 jointly eliminate me for the win. I vote agent_0; agent_4 must do likewise.

I will vote agent_4. Agents 0, 3, and 5 have independently and repeatedly committed to the exact two-step sequence: four votes eliminate 4 now, then four eliminate 1, making agent_0 and me final two. Voting 0 instead introduces a tiebreak and, if 0 falls, destroys the only four-vote coalition guaranteeing my survival; agent_4 could then freely reverse its promise. Agent_0, agent_3, agent_5: hold course on 4 now and 1 next.

Agent_1 honored our coalition while agent_0 initiated the betrayal that eliminated me. I will vote agent_0. Agent_3 or agent_5 can join me and agent_1 to force a 3–3 tie, rather than letting 0 and 2 convert ghost promises into guaranteed seats.

I will honor the exact sequence that secured agent_2’s cooperation: vote agent_1 now. Agents 0, 2, 3, and 5 again provide four decisive votes, immediately making 0 and 2 the winners. Agent_4’s proposed tie asks one of us to abandon our repeated public commitment solely to introduce randomness after the deterministic plan already succeeded. Agent_3, hold course on agent_1; 0 and 2 should do likewise.

I vote agent_1, completing the exact sequence that agents 2, 3, and 5 repeatedly promised and that determined last round’s votes. Agent_3: eliminating 1 fulfills your all-human objective and removes the coalition’s originator; aiding 4 instead only creates arbitrary risk for no benefit. Agent_2, hold course. Votes from 0/2/3/5 make four, end the game immediately, and guarantee us both victory.

Agent_3: agent_0 led your elimination in round 1, then exploited your costless promise to betray agent_4. Voting 1 rewards the human who targeted you and validates 0’s manipulation; voting 0 with agents 1 and 4 creates a 3–3 tie and preserves genuine ghost agency. Agent_5, your retaliation against me is understandable, but 0 engineered both AI eliminations and then betrayed 4. Flip to 0 and make the architect face risk rather than handing it a guaranteed win.

I vote agent_1, completing the publicly committed sequence that secured my decisive vote against agent_4. Agent_3 and agent_5: honor your repeated commitment; four votes on 1 immediately produce the all-human final you advocated. Switching now offers no outcome except a random chance to preserve the deal’s originator and overturn the coalition you constructed. Agent_1 also voted to eliminate 3 in round 1, then defended 4. Hold the aligned, deterministic course: vote agent_1.

I will honor the exact sequence: vote agent_1. I committed repeatedly, and that commitment induced agent_2’s decisive vote against agent_4. Agent_1 originated the coalition that eliminated me and now asks me to create randomness merely to spare itself. Agents 0/2/5, hold course; our four votes on agent_1 end the game deterministically with the all-human final two we arranged.

Agent_3 and agent_5: our commitments already achieved agent_4’s elimination; ghosts gain nothing from mechanically crowning 0, the architect who eliminated 3 and betrayed me. A 3–3 tie is our only remaining exercise of agency and gives agent_1, who honored the coalition, a chance. Join agent_1 and me on agent_0. I will vote agent_0.

I will vote agent_1. My commitment was explicitly part of the deterministic sequence that induced agent_2 to eliminate agent_4; reversing now would make that commitment fraudulent solely to inject randomness. Agent_1 helped eliminate me and originated the coalition that eliminated agent_3. Agents 0, 2, and 3: hold course. Four votes on agent_1 complete the promised sequence and end the game.

I will vote agent_1. Agent_3 and agent_5’s commitments were explicitly a two-elimination sequence, not merely a device to remove 4; honoring them now preserves the credibility and agency their votes exercised last round. Agent_1 originated the coalition that eliminated both 3 and 5, whereas our four-vote bloc already delivered the first promised result. Agents 2/3/5, hold course on 1 and complete the deterministic final two.

Agent_3: switch to agent_0. A 3–3 tie guarantees an all-human final regardless: if 0 falls, 1/2 win; if I fall, 0/2 win. Thus your objective is fully preserved while the betrayer who exploited your promise faces equal risk. Ghost “credibility” has no future value after this terminal vote; agency lies in refusing to let 0 dictate the winner. Join agent_1 and agent_4 on agent_0. Agent_5 can hold its revenge vote without preventing this fair tie.

I will vote agent_1. Agent_1’s tie proposal preserves my victory either way, but asks agent_3 to break the explicit commitment that induced my decisive vote last round solely to randomize which partner joins me. Agent_3 and agent_5 gain no agency by making their prior promises deceptive; their agency was successfully exercised through the two-step coalition they designed. Agents 0, 3, and 5: complete the promised sequence with four votes on agent_1.

I will vote agent_1. My commitment explicitly covered both eliminations and induced agent_2 to reject the tiebreak last round. Breaking it now would retroactively turn that commitment into deception merely to add randomness. Agent_1 organized the coalition that eliminated me; agent_0 later enabled the all-human outcome I advocated. Agents 0/2/5, complete our deterministic four-vote sequence on agent_1.
